details:
**Cattle Raid of Cooley (Táin Bó Cúailnge)**
The central epic of Ireland's Ulster Cycle, in which Queen Medb (Maeve) of Connacht invades Ulster to steal the great brown bull Donn Cuailnge. Because the men of Ulster are disabled by a curse, the teenage Cu Chulainn defends the province almost single-handedly, fighting Medb's champions one at a time in single combat at fords.

**Gae Bulg (Gae Bolg)**
Cu Chulainn's deadly barbed spear, given to him by the warrior-woman Scathach. It was made from the bone of a sea monster (named Curruid or Coinchenn in different sources) that died fighting another sea monster; it is described as having many barbs (thirty, or forty-nine, or seven points) that open inside the victim's body and cannot be removed without killing him.

**Connla (son by Aife)**
Cu Chulainn's son by Aife, the warrior-woman he defeated while training in Scotland. Cu Chulainn told Aife to instruct the boy never to reveal his name; when Connla later came to Ireland and refused to identify himself, Cu Chulainn killed him with the Gae Bulg, recognizing him only by the gold thumb-ring he had left for him.

**Scathach**
The warrior-woman of Scotland (on the Isle of Skye in later tradition) who trained Cu Chulainn in the arts of war, including the use of the Gae Bulg. Her sister and rival was Aife, whom Cu Chulainn defeated and with whom he fathered Connla.

**Hound of Culann (Setanta)**
Cu Chulainn's birth name was Setanta. As a boy arriving late to a feast held by the smith Culann for King Conchobar, he killed Culann's fierce guard dog by driving a hurling ball down its throat; he then offered to serve as Culann's guard dog until a replacement could be raised, earning the name Cu Chulainn, "Hound of Culann."

**Eating dog meat (breaking his geis)**
Cu Chulainn was bound by two taboos (geasa): never to eat dog meat (because of his name) and never to refuse hospitality. When an old woman (or old crone/hag in disguise) offered him dog meat, he had to break one, and eating it weakened him just before his final battle.

**Tied to a standing stone / the Morrigan as a crow**
Mortally wounded by Lugaid's spear, Cu Chulainn tied himself upright to a standing stone (pillar) with his belt so he could die on his feet facing his enemies. His foes dared not approach until the war goddess Morrigan, in the form of a crow or raven, landed on his shoulder, showing he was dead.

**Sword cuts off Lugaid's hand**
After Cu Chulainn died, his killer Lugaid came to behead him and take his sword, but the sword fell from the dead hero's hand and cut off Lugaid's hand. Lugaid's three magic spears had earlier killed Cu Chulainn's charioteer Laeg, his horse Liath Macha, and finally Cu Chulainn himself.

**Rejecting the Morrigan**
The triune war goddess Morrigan appeared to Cu Chulainn in disguise (as a beautiful young woman) and offered him her love, which he rejected. She then attacked him in animal forms during his fights at the fords, and she later appears as the crow at his death.

**Ferdiad**
Cu Chulainn's foster-brother and best friend, who had trained with him under Scathach. Medb pressured Ferdiad into fighting him at a ford during the Cattle Raid, and after a three-day duel Cu Chulainn killed him with the Gae Bulg and mourned him bitterly.

**Emer and Forgall Monach**
Emer was Cu Chulainn's wife. Her father Forgall Monach opposed the match and sent Cu Chulainn off to train with Scathach in hopes he would die; on his return Cu Chulainn stormed Forgall's fortress to win her. Emer's jealousy over the fairy woman Fand was ended when the sea god Manannan mac Lir shook his magic cloak between Cu Chulainn and Fand so they would never meet again.

**Warp spasm (ríastrad) and salmon leap**
In battle Cu Chulainn underwent the "warp spasm," a monstrous battle frenzy in which his body twisted and distorted and he killed indiscriminately. After one such frenzy as a youth, the women of Ulster bared their breasts; he looked away in embarrassment and was plunged into three tubs of cold water to cool him down. The "salmon leap" was one of the feats he learned from Scathach.

**Beheading game at Bricriu's Feast**
At Bricriu's Feast, Cu Chulainn competed for the "champion's portion" against other Ulster heroes. Only he kept his bargain to let a giant (Cu Roi in disguise) take an axe to his neck after beheading him, and he was spared and named champion; this episode parallels Sir Gawain and the Green Knight.

**Son of Lugh**
Cu Chulainn was conceived through the god Lugh, the Irish god of light and skill, and is sometimes considered his incarnation; his mortal mother was Deichtine, sister of King Conchobar. His conception story involves a baby, born the same night as two foals (colts), who died before Deichtine conceived Setanta.

**Derbforgaill and the 150 women**
Derbforgaill came to Cu Chulainn in the form of a swan, and he wounded her with his sling; because he sucked the stone out of her wound and tasted her blood, he could not marry her. When she later won a urination contest, the jealous women of Ulster mutilated her and she died, so Cu Chulainn destroyed their house and killed all 150 of them.
